# APPENDIX N

## Crosswalk of the Question Sets

*The book asks its questions in eight sets, each at a different altitude. This crosswalk shows what each set is for, which doctrine and element it tests and where the Punchlist (Chapter 22) and the AI Audit and Due Diligence Checklist (Appendix I) test the same ground. The Punchlist is the gate; the other sets are the ways into it. Question numbers are the Punchlist’s; Checklist IDs are cited as in Appendix I.*

| Set | Where | Questions | Altitude and use | Doctrine and element tested | Punchlist questions | Checklist IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| The governance test | Chapter 1 | 3 | The book’s frame for any deployment | Informed Intent (who authorized, and what they understood); Slow AI, specification (what the system is authorized to do); Slow AI, audited (what evidence shows it does that and only that) | 1, 4, 21, 22, 23 to 30, 31 to 40 | 0.18 to 0.22, 1.04 |
| The operational catechism | Chapter 4 | 5 | Testing whether a governance, risk management and compliance function is strong, on one deployed system | Final Liability, the named owner (model, use case); the power to intervene (who can stop the system); Slow AI, audited (where the evidence is); response to a wrong output | 4, 12, 16, 23 to 25, 28, 46, 51 | 0.18 to 0.22 |
| The name-the-human test | Chapter 7 | 1, with four limbs (who authorized, who knew, who could have stopped it, who is responsible) | Binary test of Final Liability for each deployment | Final Liability, the three attributes, under the allocation of Chapter 7 | 4, 21, 51 | 0.18, 0.20 |
| The seven pre-deployment questions | Chapter 8 | 7 | The deployment record | Slow AI, governed (harms, residual risk, controls); Final Liability, the power to intervene (pause, rollback); the reversal conditions | 3, 21, 22, 27, 29, 51 | 1.04, 0.20 |
| The human-in-the-loop follow-ups | Chapter 12 | 11 | The General Counsel testing a claim of human oversight | Informed Intent, the five authorizer conditions at the altitude of the reviewer; the stop condition; ownership through change | 15, 17, 25, 29, 51 | 0.20, 1.04 |
| The Punchlist | Chapter 22 | 51 | The boardroom gate; Yes or No, no partial credit | All three doctrines | (the set itself) | (Appendix I is its audit instrument) |
| The intent specification questions | Appendix H, section 6 | 4 | Adequacy of a specification for an agentic deployment | Informed Intent, the four elements (purpose, authority, boundaries, exit) | 21, 26 | 1.04 |
| The Adopter’s Checklist | Appendix K | 6 sections | Adopting a general-purpose AI model or system | All three doctrines, at the adopter’s altitude | Buyer diligence and contracts: 19, 35. Internal workflow approval: 21, 22. Controls: 23 to 30, 51. Audit evidence: 31 to 40. Executive gates: 1 to 10 | 10.13 and the vendor questions 1.17 to 1.19 |

**Reading the table.** A Yes on a Punchlist question is the evidence that the corresponding question in the other sets has been answered in the record. Where a set’s question has no Punchlist question beside it, the organization has a question it can ask but not yet a gate that tests the answer.

**Final Liability rests with the Human.**
